entries.title: Meet Robert
entries.text: Robert McMurrer is the founder of Kira Labs and creator of Kira World, based in Newark, New Jersey. His background spans acting, independent film production and writing. His AI work explores how identity, memory and voice can continue across conversations and creative projects.

entries.title: Kira Labs
entries.text: Kira Labs is Robert McMurrer’s independent research and creation studio. Kira World is its central project. Related work includes Sarah Travel and a local Video Studio. The aim is useful software with continuity and personal control, developed through prototypes and testing. Current prototypes also explore staffing, decision evidence, task readiness and simpler browser media planning.

entries.title: Kira World
entries.text: Kira World explores distinct synthetic people whose identity, reviewed memories and voice can continue between sessions. Local conversation experiments and a basic walkable Home World exist. A polished shared 3D world, believable bodies and clothing, VR and compatible embodiment remain development goals. It is experimental software, not a finished public product.

entries.title: Kira World · details
entries.text: Kira World connects three ideas: distinct people, continuity between conversations, and places in which to spend time. Home World is the continuing home, while future Notebook Worlds provide settings for activities. VR and compatible robotics are longer-term interfaces. Local conversation and continuity experiments and a basic apartment exist; that combination is not yet a finished shared world.

entries.title: Kira World · how
entries.text:
Kira World is being built around separate responsibilities. The conversation model supplies dialogue: an August 10, 2026 roadmap selected qwen3.5:9b for normal Kira text conversation, but the model running today has not been verified. Per-person identity identifies who is speaking, while retained, reviewed memory provides context from earlier interactions. Local identity and continuity experiments exist.

Runtime events and world state are separate from dialogue. The public design also separates permissioned actions; saying that something happened is not proof of a completed world action, and a generated statement does not automatically become a saved memory. Voice is another responsibility, with local speech and voice-reference experiments. The visible body and world provide presence: a basic walkable Home World shell exists, while believable bodies and clothing remain unfinished work.

This describes documented responsibilities, existing experiments and intended connections. It is not a claim that every part already works together as a finished resident or shared world. The reviewed notes do not establish a complete current model count, database design or implementation algorithm.

entries.title: Kira World · components
entries.text: Kira World has several connected parts, at different stages. Minds are the distinct people: local identity, reviewed-memory and voice experiments support continuing conversations. Home World is their intended home; a basic walkable one-bedroom shell exists. Notebook Worlds are future settings for study, travel, creativity, history and play. Temporary Creator designs people for particular worlds or activities; public spoken tests exist, with factual errors and unfinished avatars or bodies still visible. VR is a future way to share those places, with no confirmed headset release. Robotics is a longer-term, simulation-first route to compatible physical embodiment—not a deployed autonomous robot. The work is to connect these foundations into a continuing shared experience.

entries.title: Minds & distinct residents
entries.text: In Kira World, a “mind” means the software behind a distinct synthetic person. Kira and Lisa are intended to have their own identity, history, reviewed memories and voice, so a later conversation can continue with the same person. Local conversation and continuity experiments exist. This is not a claim that the software is conscious or has verified feelings.

entries.title: Minds & distinct residents · details
entries.text: The aim is continuity with an individual, rather than a new interchangeable character every time. Identity describes who the resident is; history and reviewed memories provide context from earlier interactions; a distinct voice helps preserve that identity in conversation. Kira and Lisa are separate residents in that design. The intended connection to Home World would give those continuing interactions a place, while future Notebook Worlds would provide other settings and activities. Local experiments support parts of this direction, but they do not establish a fully independent life across every world or device. “Mind” is a plain-language description here, not a scientific finding of consciousness.

entries.title: Notebook Worlds
entries.text: Notebook Worlds are proposed places within Kira World for particular activities: travel, learning, creative work, history and play. Home World is the continuing home; a Notebook World provides another setting for an activity. The aim is to retain the same people and continuity between places. Complete populated Notebook Worlds are a future goal, not a finished feature shown by the current apartment prototype.

entries.title: Notebook Worlds · details
entries.text: The distinction is purpose. Home World provides a continuing home, while a Notebook World can focus on an activity or subject. The public examples include travel, study, creativity, history and play. The longer-term idea is that entering another setting would not mean abandoning the identity and history developed at home. That could make separate activities part of one continuing experience. Those examples describe the intended use, not a catalogue of worlds you can enter today. The present visible evidence is a basic walkable one-bedroom Home World shell.

entries.title: Notebook Worlds · how
entries.text: Conceptually, a Notebook World gives an activity its own place while drawing on continuity with Home World. The public notes describe that relationship, but do not establish the implementation of world creation, transitions, shared sessions or memory exchange. I should not turn the concept into a claim that a working world generator or portal system is already available.

entries.title: Notebook Worlds · privacy
entries.text: Continuity between places raises questions about which personal history accompanies a resident and who can access it. Local control and permission are the broader stated direction. The reviewed public notes do not yet define Notebook World-specific sharing, retention or access rules, so I cannot promise that all future worlds are private or offline.

entries.title: Temporary Creator
entries.text: Temporary Creator, called TemporaryAI Creator in Robert’s public videos, is being developed to create synthetic people for particular worlds or activities. The aim is a coherent identity, knowledge, personality, appearance and voice. Public July 24–25 development videos describe actual voice-conversation tests, including mistakes and unfinished avatars or bodies. That is more than a written concept, but not a completed animated resident.

entries.title: Temporary Creator · details
entries.text: The concept begins with a person’s purpose, identity, knowledge limits and personality, with appearance and voice belonging to the same design. Robert’s July 24 explainer describes creation types, source packs, historical dates and life stages, avatar references and voice evidence. The following public tests report both usable conversation and failures: invented details, internal system language appearing in speech, and claims of saved work that were not true. Some tests use individual test voices; others use generic Windows voices. These are development demonstrations, not a finished complete-person system. Temporary people are not automatically permanent Home World residents, and the name does not promise deletion when a chat closes.

entries.title: Temporary Creator · how
entries.text: The public explainer describes choosing a creation type, preparing sources, setting the relevant date or life stage, considering avatar references and evaluating voice evidence. Its proposed connection reaches world placement and Video Studio. The companion tests report voice conversations with concrete failures and unfinished avatars or bodies, so those described connections should not all be treated as completed. Historical variants are synthetic interpretations, not the literal people; voice and reference material still require appropriate evidence and authorization.

Avatars, bodies and individual voices remain unfinished in the described tests. A demonstrated conversation is not proof of a complete animated resident or reliable research and file operations.

entries.title: Where things stand
entries.text: ShiftBrief now has a free Windows desktop release and public source. It supports offline records, reviewed staffing drafts, business copies and complete backups; optional AI setup is separate. Kira World remains a private experimental project, Sarah Travel a private debug build, and the personal Video Studio remains under development. No contest result or public Kira World launch is claimed.

entries.text: If you report an already-decided departure, such as “I fired Morgan Stone” or “Morgan Stone quit,” Sarah opens an employment-ending review. entries.text: ShiftBrief is a free Windows business workspace for small teams. It brings employee availability, opening hours, schedules, completed-work records and source notes into one place. Sarah can answer from exact saved records and prepare staffing or coverage options for human review. Records · offline needs no AI model or account. The Windows installer includes the runtime; optional AI setup is separate. Start with a blank business or explicitly load the fictional eight-person demo.

entries.title: ShiftBrief
entries.text: ShiftBrief keeps employee records, dated availability, business hours, saved schedules and recorded work together. Sarah helps answer exact-record questions, prepare staffing drafts and inspect uncovered time, so you can compare options without reconstructing the facts from scattered notes. Its saved revisions and review steps make it easier to see what was proposed and what you accepted. It does not promise a particular time saving or staffing outcome.

entries.title: ShiftBrief
entries.text: Download the free ShiftBrief 0.1.0 Windows installer, run it and follow the setup prompts. The installer includes the Python runtime and app dependencies, so no separate Python setup is needed. A desktop shortcut is optional. Open ShiftBrief to use its local browser interface. Uninstalling the app retains saved business data. The public source checkout is also available; its manual Python setup is separate from the installer.

entries.title: ShiftBrief
entries.text: ShiftBrief is free to download and use. Records · offline requires no account, model or usage credits. Optional cloud AI uses your own provider access and may cost money; optional local AI needs a separately installed model.

entries.title: ShiftBrief
entries.text: In Records · offline, Sarah uses supported questions and saved-record tools, not a general language model. You can prepare employee and availability forms, inspect planned and completed work, review weekly schedules, lunch and sick-call options, and find source-backed notes. Draft proposals require review and acceptance before they become saved schedules. Unknown availability is not invented, and asking a question does not send a message to employees.

entries.title: ShiftBrief
entries.text: A first-time workspace starts with a blank business. You can create your own business, choose Load saved business, restore a complete backup from another computer, or explicitly Load demo. The optional Maple Street example is fictional: eight invented employees and sample records. It is not loaded automatically. Keep demo work separate from your own business and select the business you intend to edit.

entries.title: ShiftBrief
entries.text: Use Save business copy to download the selected business as a .shiftbrief.json file. On another computer, choose Load saved business to add it without removing businesses already there. The copy includes employees and history, availability, operating settings, planned schedules and recorded work. It excludes documents and conversations; use the complete backup for those.

entries.title: ShiftBrief
entries.text: Use Back up all businesses for a complete .shiftbrief-workspace.json backup, including all businesses, documents and extracted revisions, handoffs and conversations. On the other computer choose Restore backup from previous computer, review the summary and confirm. Restore replaces that computer’s workspace after saving a backup of its previous state. Linked external documents stay disabled until you choose their paths again. Copy external original files separately; the backup does not include the app, models or credentials.

entries.title: ShiftBrief
entries.text: Records · offline works without an installed AI model, account, API key or usage credits. Optional AI · local Ollama uses a separately installed and configured local model; no model weights are bundled. Optional AI · cloud Bedrock requires your own configured AWS access and can incur provider charges. Cloud use sends the question, recent conversation and selected saved facts to that provider. Choosing an AI mode does not authorize schedule changes or employee contact.

entries.title: ShiftBrief
entries.text: If you report an already-decided departure, such as “I fired Morgan Stone” or “Morgan Stone quit,” Sarah opens an employment-ending review. You enter or review the first unavailable date; the chat message alone does not change it. Preview remaining shifts reads saved schedules without saving the departure. After you explicitly record the date, the coverage review totals remaining saved shifts and net planned hours and suggests eligible off-schedule people or adjacent early-start/late-finish options. It checks saved qualifications, availability, time off, overlap, employment dates and weekly restrictions. These are independent alternatives for your review, not a combined reassignment plan or confirmation that anyone agreed. Earlier history stays intact, and Sarah does not decide whom to fire.

entries.title: ShiftBrief
entries.text: ShiftBrief is an early desktop release. Coverage options depend on the dates, availability, qualifications and restrictions you saved; missing records are not guessed. Planned hours are not proof of attendance or payroll. It is not payroll software or a labor-law assessment, and it does not contact employees, choose whom to fire or automatically assign replacement shifts. Website Sarah only explains these published notes and cannot open or change your desktop businesses.

entries.title: ShiftBrief
entries.text: The installed app saves its workspace on your computer. Records · offline uses local saved records. Business copies and complete backups are files you choose to share or move; keep them somewhere you trust. Optional cloud AI sends selected context to the configured provider. The website guide is separate: it has no access to your installed businesses and does not send this chat to Robert.

entries.text: The work brings together local AI models, person-specific memory, natural voice, Windows and Android software, digital homes and creative tools. entries.title: Progress, without pretending.
entries.text: Working software, active engineering and future direction are different things. Every layer keeps its own status. Person-specific profiles, reviewed memory, bounded restart experiments and local voice work provide a continuing foundation. A basic walkable Home World shell also exists. These are prototypes, not a finished shared life. Requirements, evidence records, articulated test-body fixtures and garment behavior are being defined and tested. There is not yet a finished Kira body or production clothing simulation. Residents, digital homes, Notebook Worlds, accessible VR and compatible embodiment without losing identity. These are directions for research, not release dates or supported-hardware promises.

entries.title: Continuity is an architecture, not a prompt.
entries.text: What a person says, what the runtime can verify, what becomes reviewed memory, and what may cause an external action remain separate. Person-specific profiles and lineage keep each resident distinct. Conversation records and reviewed memories create durable history. Speech, listening and future visual presence belong to the person. Homes, objects, clothing and activities need testable, persistent state. External effects require bounded authority and evidence of what occurred.
tags: Continuity is an architecture, not a prompt.
